terravera.sterilization.boiling.name: Boiling in a Pot
terravera.sterilization.boiling.desc: Hold a filled container against a TFC firepit pot that is at or above 100C and the water inside is marked boiled. The clay pot is one of the first things a TFC player builds, so the complete answer to waterborne disease is available on day one - for the price of fuel, every single time.
terravera.sterilization.rolling_boil.des: The sustained version of boiling. A brief boil is not a boil: keep the pot rolling for a full five minutes and even the hardiest cysts - Giardia and Cryptosporidium - are dead. TerraVera treats any pot boiled to 100C as having had the full rolling boil.
terravera.sterilization.rolling_boil.mat: Clay pot, firepit, and enough fuel for a sustained burn.
terravera.sterilization.pasteurization.d: Hold a pot hot but below the boil and the water is pasteurized: most bacteria and viruses die, but the tough protozoan cysts survive. It is what you get when you cannot quite reach a boil - better than nothing, never as good as boiling.
terravera.sterilization.stone_boiling.de: Drop fire-heated stones into a container of water. The stones carry their heat into the water and raise it past pasteurization without a pot over the fire. The classic no-pot trick; use the Boiling Stones on a filled container.
terravera.sterilization.stone_boiling.ma: Boiling Stones (rocks heated in a TFC kiln or forge), any water container.
terravera.sterilization.sodis.name: SODIS - Solar Water Disinfection
terravera.sterilization.sodis.desc: Glass bottles on a rack, tilted into the sun. Six hours of clear daylight lets the UV in sunlight do the disinfection - free, fireless, and one of the great emergency methods. The SODIS Rack needs clear sky and daylight to process.
terravera.sterilization.sodis.materials: SODIS Rack, glass bottles, a clear day.
terravera.sterilization.solar_still.name: Solar Still Distillation
terravera.sterilization.solar_still.desc: The passive Solar Still collector condenses vapour, so the water it produces has effectively been distilled by the sun. It is slow - one bucket per long day - but the water that comes out is as clean as water gets.
terravera.sterilization.solar_still.mate: Solar Still collector, open sky, daylight.
terravera.sterilization.distillation.des: Boil water in the copper still and condense the steam back down. Nothing survives the round trip; the distillate is the cleanest water in the game. Costs copper, fuel, and time - the still is the mid-game answer.
terravera.sterilization.cloth_filter.des: Fold any woven cloth - burlap, linen, a shirt - and pour through it. It catches grit, mud, and the biggest parasites. It is the cheapest method in the catalogue and exactly as good as that suggests.
terravera.sterilization.cloth_filter.mat: Burlap or linen cloth, cordage, a container.
The TerraVera water filter: sand and charcoal in a frame. It removes the protozoa and most of the load, but leaves the bacteria - cholera and typhoid go straight through it. The field answer; boiling is still the camp answer.
Water Filter item: sand, charcoal, cordage, cloth.
terravera.sterilization.bio_sand.name: Bio-Sand Filtration
terravera.sterilization.bio_sand.desc: A barrel of graded sand and gravel with a living layer of organisms on top. The biology eats the pathogens while gravity pulls the water through. The Bio-Sand Filter is the cheap always-on workhorse of a settled camp.
terravera.sterilization.bio_sand.materia: Bio-Sand Filter block: sand, gravel, burlap, cordage.
terravera.sterilization.ceramic_filter.d: A fired clay candle with pores small enough to strain out bacteria. Fragile, but reusable for a very long time if rinsed. The candle starts as an unfired clay piece and must go through a TFC kiln.
terravera.sterilization.ceramic_filter.m: Ceramic Filter Candle (fired from clay in a TFC kiln).
terravera.sterilization.settling.name: Settling / Sedimentation
terravera.sterilization.settling.desc: Let the water stand and the mud falls out, taking a surprising fraction of the load with it. The Clarifier Tank does it properly, with a slow paddle and an overflow spout. It never fully sterilizes - but it makes everything else work better.
terravera.sterilization.flocculation.des: Stir in alum and the suspended particles clump into flakes heavy enough to sink, dragging pathogens down with them. The method real water-treatment plants use; the Alum Crystals do it for one container at a time.
terravera.sterilization.flocculation.mat: Alum Crystals, a container, and time to settle.
terravera.sterilization.moringa.name: Moringa Seed Powder
terravera.sterilization.moringa.desc: Crushed moringa seeds are a traditional flocculant used across Africa and Asia for thousands of years. The powder makes the fine particles clump and settle, exactly like alum but from a seed.
terravera.sterilization.moringa.material: Moringa Seed Powder, a container, and time to settle.
terravera.sterilization.chlorination.des: Chlorine is the world's default answer to bad water: cheap, fast, and lethal to bacteria and viruses. Its one famous weakness is Cryptosporidium, which shrugs it off - boil if you can.
terravera.sterilization.chlorination.mat: Chlorine Tablets (salt, lye, and charcoal, boiled in a TFC pot).
terravera.sterilization.iodination.name: Iodine Disinfection
terravera.sterilization.iodination.desc: Iodine tincture, a few drops per litre. The backpacker's classic: light, fast, reliable against bacteria and viruses. Leave it to work, and expect the taste.
terravera.sterilization.iodination.mater: Iodine Tincture (wood ash and salt, boiled in a TFC pot).
terravera.sterilization.permanganate.des: A strong oxidizer sold as deep-purple crystals. A few crystals turn the water pink and kill most pathogens; the water will taste of iron afterwards. A standard field-kit method.
terravera.sterilization.permanganate.mat: Permanganate Crystals (charcoal and salt, boiled in a TFC pot).
terravera.sterilization.acidification.de: The emergency field trick: sour the water hard and wait. Acid slows most bacteria down - it buys you time on the trail, not safety. The last resort that is still a real method.
terravera.sterilization.acidification.ma: Sour Citrus Juice (citrus or TFC vinegar).
terravera.sterilization.silver.name: Colloidal Silver
terravera.sterilization.silver.desc: Silver ions are mildly antimicrobial and - uniquely among chemical methods - keep working for days, which makes silver-treated water stay good in storage. Slow, mild, persistent.
terravera.sterilization.silver.materials: Colloidal Silver (silver ingot and salt, boiled in a TFC pot).
terravera.sterilization.uv.name: Ultraviolet Sterilization
terravera.sterilization.uv.desc: A UV lamp in a glass chamber. The radiation shreds the DNA of almost everything that passes through - bacteria, viruses, protozoa. A few exceptionally tough spores survive, which is why RO and distillation still outrank it.
terravera.sterilization.uv.materials: UV Sterilizer block (iron, glass, an RO membrane).
Force the water through a membrane whose pores are smaller than anything alive. The Reverse-Osmosis Membrane item does it for one container at a time - the most thorough portable filter that exists.
Reverse-Osmosis Membrane (wrought-iron sheets and burlap). A full machine version is planned.
terravera.sterilization.freezing.name: Freezing and Melting
terravera.sterilization.freezing.desc: Water that froze and then melted carries far less than the water it came from - the ice crystals exclude the pathogens. It is not sterilization: some bacteria survive the freeze. Cold, high, running water is simply the safest natural source there is.
terravera.sterilization.freezing.materia: A hard winter. The TerraVera disease system already models cold water as cleaner.
